$comment: Finding-level recurrence ledger. RECURRENCE.md is GENERATED from this file by
scripts/feedback/recurrence.ts (run via `pnpm regen`) — edit this, never the markdown.
THE BINDING RULE: `status: closed` requires a non-empty `guard`, and that guard must
resolve to a real package.json script or a real file. 'Fixed in source' is not a
closure — a fix with nothing holding it in place is how twelve reports kept
re-reporting the same findings. If no guard can express the invariant, keep the
finding open with `guard: null` and a `guardNote` saying why; the next plan lists it.

findings.title: Vendored source fails the adopter's strict lint/type toolchain
findings.note: Closed only once the guard ran the adopter's REAL toolchain. The previous guard (lint:host-strict, oxlint) was written for this exact finding and could not express the rules that fired: it found 0, real ESLint found 501.

findings.title: Documented ESLint entry point is the legacy eslintrc shape, applies no rules
findings.note: Same fact lived in three places and was wrong in two — plus a fourth nobody had checked: the CLI's own `cascivo create` scaffold. eslint.config.js in the fixture is now the single owner.

findings.title: A manifest requires @cascivo/components, which is private and unpublishable
findings.guardNote: npm-dependency-reality — specced in WS-1, not yet written.

findings.title: The documented theming API ships only in @cascivo/react, unreachable on the copy-paste path
findings.note: The theme runtime moved to @cascivo/core (with persistedSignal and the sync drivers, which had to move too or core->storage->core would cycle); @cascivo/react re-exports every name unchanged, so Path B sees no difference. path-a-parity is the twin of the path-b-parity guard that already existed: only one direction had ever been built, which is why this was invisible. It also fails when a doc names a Path-B-only API without saying so — the half that would actually have caught this.

findings.title: Badge maps `neutral` to the brand accent while Tag, Status and Notification do not
findings.note: Badge neutral now maps to the subtle look, matching Tag/Status/Notification; the accent look stays reachable as variant="primary". tone-parity asserts each canonical tone reads from its own token family in all four components, and that neutral is never accent/primary. It checks families rather than exact tokens, because each component legitimately presents tone differently (filled chip, quiet chip, dot, tinted card).

findings.title: ChartFrame's measured-height signal is unreachable, so charts overflow fixed cells
findings.note: ChartFrame's `height` no longer defaults to 300 in the destructure, so `fixedHeight ?? height.value` finally reads the measured signal; the frame is a shrinkable flex item so a constrained parent can hand the plot the space left after the legend. Every pre-existing ChartFrame test passed an explicit height — the one case that was never broken — so the new tests cover the omitted-height path and were demonstrated failing against the old default. computed:check cannot cover this: it renders static markup with no hydration, so no ResizeObserver ever runs.

findings.title: Meter carries the shared responsive-width doc but never uses ChartFrame
findings.note: Checks the CLAIM, not the shape: a chart whose `width` doc promises container tracking must reach useChartSize (directly or via ChartFrame) and carry a viewBox. A 'must import ChartFrame' rule would have forced Meter — which has no data points and needs none of the frame's tooltip/zoom machinery — into a worse design. Found two more beyond the report: sparkline and bullet both carried the responsive boilerplate while hard-coding a width default, and sparkline's documented default (80) did not match its code (120).

findings.title: The CLI installs bare package names and resolves to a stale lockfile entry
findings.note: installCommand pins every @cascivo/* to an explicit specifier (@latest, or the registry floor widened to an installable range), with a --pin escape hatch. Non-cascivo packages stay bare — their version is the app's business. installHint delegates to the same function, so the printed recovery command is exactly what the CLI runs; a recovery command that differs from the failed one is a trap.

findings.title: `cascivo doctor` prints 'No violations found' without running the drift check
findings.note: runDoctorDrift now returns a DriftOutcome, so the default `cascivo doctor` runs it and can still say something honest: when drift cannot run (no lockfile, unreachable registry) it prints 'drift: not checked — <reason>' rather than an unqualified clean. --drift keeps its meaning as drift-only. Also adds a formatter-drift finding for the projects that predate `init` writing the exclusion.

findings.title: Continuously-deployed docs describe a layer order the published packages do not have
findings.guardNote: Specced in WS-8a: generate the layer statement from layers.css, and version-stamp llms.txt so a reader can tell what it describes.

findings.title: @types/react version skew changes which assertions and refs type-check
findings.guardNote: Carried forward from the 07-28 plan §0.5, where the fixture DISPROVED the original diagnosis. Still open there; untouched by the 08-06 plan.

findings.title: A deprecated component is only marked in source, after the adopter has vendored it
findings.note: ComponentMeta now carries `deprecated`, so list/add/MCP/docs all render it at discovery time. The guard asserts the replacement resolves, entry and manifest agree, and each surface reads the field — not merely that the type has it.

findings.title: Vendored source carries dead bindings the adopter's first `tsc --noEmit` reports
findings.note: noUnusedLocals/noUnusedParameters on, matching the official TanStack Start scaffolder. Found 11, not the 1 reported: five leftover useSignal imports from the useEffectPropSignal migration, a discarded fetchRegistry network call in `cascivo generate`, a fillColor() taking min/max and ignoring them, and SkipNavLink wrapped in forwardRef while never attaching the ref — consumers got null with no type error, and ref-parity had counted it compliant because it checks the wrapper, not the wiring.

findings.title: Tabs cannot render links; Menu reads children positionally; Link doubles its external arrow
findings.note: TabsTrigger gains asChild (aschild-docs forces the router-guide entry). Menu and ContextMenu partition children by component identity with a dev-time error naming the contract — which immediately caught a preact-compat test that passed `trigger`/`items` props Menu does not have, rendered nothing, and had been asserting 'no console error' about an empty tree. Link suppresses its generated arrow via :has() when the link ends in its own icon. Barrels are generated for all 138 component dirs, so the 6-of-132 half-convention is gone.
